paragraphs: Mentioned in Bamidbar Rabbah 16:24. Hyman calls this a scribal error: the statement appears in Eichah Rabbah on ‘What shall I testify to you?’ and, in his citation, in Pesikta Rabbati, chapter 10, under the name R' Huna of Tzippori. In Shemot Rabbah 45:2 it is in R' Shimon bar Yochai's name.

notes.text: The first Midrash Rabbah volume and printed locator פט״ז-כר remain unresolved. The other references give differing personal attributions, not an automatic identity equation.

The first Rabbah work and supplied פט״ז-כר remain unidentified; no guessed16:24 is substituted. Earlier Bamidbar16 nonmatch and Huna/Tanchuma searches are finite inherited reports, not freshly read whole chapters or statements. Hyman calls the attribution a scribal error at full force; Eichah/Pesikta/Shemot comparisons remain his argument, not established correction history or a single identity. ShimonbarYochai is the contextual רשב״י expansion, but these exact abbreviated personal titles remain R' without new title evidence.

Hyman’s printed notice (vol. II, p. 574) cites Bamidbar Rabbah 16:24 and Shemot Rabbah 45:2, where the supplied transcription has different numerals. Bamidbar names Yehudah of Tzippori, Eikhah Rabbah 2:17 names Huna of Tzippori, and Shemot credits the corresponding saying to Shimon bar Yochai, with Chanin of Tzippori credited separately. A parallel in the consulted Pesikta Rabbati chapter 21 names Huna Rabba of Tzippori. The basis of Hyman’s chapter 10 citation is unresolved. These parallels document different attributions; the judgment that the first is a scribal error is Hyman’s.
